description: PaperScope curated AI and computer architecture terminology

senses.en: A mechanism that assigns different weights to information when forming a representation.
A model that predicts each element conditioned on preceding elements.
Intermediate reasoning steps produced or used by a model.
Representation learning that draws related examples together and separates unrelated examples.
A generative model that learns to reverse a gradual noising process.
Coordinated computation, storage, and scheduling across edge devices and cloud infrastructure.
Intelligence grounded in perception and action through a physical or simulated body.
Learning or adapting from a small number of examples.
Adapting a pretrained model to a task or domain using additional training.
A broadly trained model that can be adapted to many downstream tasks.

zh: 模型生成的不实或无依据内容
senses.en: A fluent model output that is unsupported, incorrect, or fabricated.
An apparent perception without an external stimulus.
Task adaptation through examples or instructions in the prompt without parameter updates.
Training a compact student model to reproduce behavior learned by a larger teacher.
A language model with large-scale parameters and broad text capabilities.
An architecture that routes inputs to a subset of specialized expert networks.
Involving multiple autonomous agents that cooperate, compete, or coordinate.
Learning from or jointly representing more than one data modality.
A reinforcement-learning method that directly optimizes policy parameters.
Designing prompts to elicit reliable and useful model behavior.
Learning behavior from interactions, rewards, and delayed consequences.
Generation conditioned on information retrieved from an external corpus.
A model that estimates preferences or utility for candidate outputs.
Faster generation by proposing tokens with a draft model and verifying them in parallel.
Additional computation allocated while solving an input at inference time.
Moving computation from one device or execution location to another.
A model that jointly processes visual and linguistic information.
Predicting a control-flow branch outcome or target before it is resolved.
Rules that keep multiple cached copies of shared data mutually consistent.
Multiple cache levels arranged by latency, capacity, and proximity to processors.
A modular die designed to be integrated with other dies in one package.
Hardware specialized for a constrained family of workloads.
Stacked memory providing wide interfaces and high aggregate bandwidth.
The software-visible contract of a processor, including instructions, registers, and memory behavior.
Rules governing the order in which memory operations become visible to processors.
Storage levels organized to balance access latency, capacity, bandwidth, and cost.
Computation placed close to memory to reduce data movement.
An on-chip communication fabric connecting cores, caches, and accelerators.
A memory organization where access latency depends on processor and memory location.
Executing instructions when operands and resources are ready rather than strictly in program order.
Performing operations within or directly alongside memory arrays.
Repeated DRAM row activation that can induce bit flips in adjacent rows.
An unintended information channel based on timing, power, cache state, or other observable effects.
Issuing instructions from multiple hardware threads in the same processor cycle.
A regular array of processing elements that rhythmically passes data between neighbors.
A cache of recent virtual-to-physical address translations.
